article_title: Istio 1.31.2, 1.30.6 and 1.29.9 Patch an AuthorizationPolicy Method-Case Bypass Over HTTP/2 and an Ambient-Mode istiod Crash

content_preview.title: Istio 1.31.2, 1.30.6 and 1.29.9 Patch an AuthorizationPolicy Method-Case Bypass Over HTTP/2 and an Ambient-Mode istiod Crash
content_preview.summary: Istio's patch releases fix a High-severity AuthorizationPolicy bypass over HTTP/2 (CVSS 7.4) and a mesh-wide istiod crash in ambient mode (CVSS 7.7), per GitHub advisories.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Istio has shipped patch releases 1.31.2, 1.30.6 and 1.29.9 that fix two vulnerabilities in the service mesh itself. According to the [GitHub security advisory](https://github.com/istio/istio/security/advisories/GHSA-w44g-8m76-8gc5), one lets requests slip past `AuthorizationPolicy` method rules over HTTP/2 by changing the case of the method. The [second advisory](https://github.com/istio/istio/security/advisories/GHSA-7p2q-4xvg-vxc6) describes a way for a tenant to crash the istiod ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (633 words, range 400-1200). Leads with the two Istio fixes, gives mechanics, versions, mitigations, then a clearly separated Envoy section and a What We Don't Know section. No AI self-reference, neutral tone.
editor_notes.source_verification: All four sources are first-party GitHub security advisories (document). Snapshots source-0..3.html.gz returned 200 with full advisory text (no suspicious_patterns in manifest for any source); I additionally re-fetched each advisory via the GitHub REST API (repos/<org>/<repo>/security-advisories/<GHSA>) and verified every field against the structured data. (1) GHSA-w44g-8m76-8gc5 (istio): 'AuthorizationPolicy method rules are bypassed over HTTP/2 by changing the method case'; high; CVSS 3.1 7.4 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N; no CVE; no CWE listed (article does not state one); published 2026-10-16; reporter izzysec; vulnerable ranges >=1.29.0,<1.29.9 / >=1.30.0,<1.30.6 / >=1.31.0,<1.31.2, patched 1.29.9/1.30.6/1.31.2. Quotes verified verbatim: 'is compiled to a case-sensitive `:method` matcher.', 'because the codec rejects non-uppercase methods before authorization.', 'Same class as CVE-2021-39155 (case-sensitive host matching).' Workaround (ALLOW with explicit methods allow-list) accurate. Mechanics correct: DENY+methods or ALLOW+notMethods compiled to case-sensitive :method matcher; HTTP/2 lowercase method does not match and is forwarded; HTTP/1.1 unaffected. (2) GHSA-7p2q-4xvg-vxc6 (istio): 'istiod crash (DoS) when a ServiceEntry claims an IP-addressed waypoint's address'; high; CVSS 3.1 7.7 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:N/A:H; CWE-248 (not stated in article); no CVE; published 2026-10-16; reporter yshch; same three ranges and patched versions 1.29.9/1.30.6/1.31.2, so BOTH Istio advisories are fixed in all three releases as the title implies. Trigger verified: ServiceEntry spec.addresses set to the waypoint ClusterIP in any namespace -> krt FetchOne panics ('FetchOne found for more than 1 item') -> crash-loop until ServiceEntry deleted; impact (tenant with ServiceEntry-create can crash istiod mesh-wide, config distribution and cert rotation stall) and three workarounds match; ambient mode with IP-addressed waypoint only. (3) GHSA-8vc2-jrm4-835w (envoy): OAuth2 filter null deref via path-less CONNECT; high; CVSS 7.5 (article states no score, only 'high' - correct); CWE-476; no CVE; published 2026-10-06; vulnerable >=1.16.0,<1.40.0; patched 1.36.12 1.37.8 1.38.6 1.39.3; fix 'rejects requests without a :path header with a 400 Bad Request local reply' accurate; unauthenticated single-request process crash accurate. (4) GHSA-47vj-9r25-wv5j (envoy): api_key_auth filter crash on path-less CONNECT when hiding credentials; medium; CVSS 6.5 (article states 6.5, correct); PR:L - requires a valid API key (article states this, correct); CWE-476; no CVE; published 2026-10-06; patched same four versions (article correct). Envoy/Istio relationship: neither Istio advisory mentions Envoy or the Envoy advisories, and the Envoy advisories do not mention Istio; the article makes no causal claim, labels the Envoy items 'Separately' and states bundled Envoy builds are not covered by the cited advisories. The section heading 'Related Envoy advisories' is topical only (the Envoy advisories are 'related' to each other per their own references) and the body does not assert an upstream link, so no correction is needed. The Istio advisories link istio.io (istio-security-2026-007) in their references; the article does not cite or rely on istio.io (verified: all 4 body links are in article.sources, no orphan or extra URLs). Istio release tags 1.31.2 (2026-10-16), 1.30.6 and 1.29.9 (2026-10-15) exist on GitHub, consistent with the article.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, version, CVSS score/vector, severity label, date (October 6) and quote traced to the advisories; no discrepancies. 'Both are rated High' correct for the Istio advisories. 'What We Don't Know' is accurate: none of the four advisories carries a CVE id, none claims exploitation in the wild, and the Istio advisories give ranges only for 1.29-1.31. The summary's 'mesh-wide istiod crash' matches the advisory impact text.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributed throughout; severity stated as the advisories rate it.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Istio security coverage in the archive (Istio appears only in passing in Kubernetes ingress/Gateway API pieces). Related prior piece: Envoy 1.40.0 release article (2026-10/17); the OAuth2 advisory lists 1.40.0 as outside the vulnerable range, but this article does not claim otherwise. Not a duplicate.
concerns: The 'Related Envoy advisories' section is only loosely tied to the Istio fixes; the article handles this honestly by disclaiming any bundling relationship.
The article does not mention the CWE (CWE-248 on the ambient advisory; none on the method-case advisory); optional detail only.
recommendations: Consider noting the date the advisories were published (October 16) and that the Istio advisories link a security bulletin on istio.io (not citable under the allowlist).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced first-party security coverage with no corrections needed; word count 633, validate and link checks clean. Featured candidacy: 2 - Istio is a widely deployed service mesh and one issue is an AuthorizationPolicy enforcement bypass (High, 7.4), but the bypass is limited to HTTP/2 DENY/notMethods rules and the crash needs ServiceEntry-create rights in ambient mode with IP-addressed waypoints, so it is significant for a defined platform audience rather than industry-changing.
